claims.text: GDACS assessed Tropical Cyclone SAUDEL-26 at an Overall Orange alert (medium humanitarian impact), with peak sustained winds of 213 km/h (Category 4) and approximately 3.5 million people exposed to Category 1 (120 km/h) or higher winds across the Northern Mariana Islands, Japan and China; the event window runs 18-24 August 2026, with a maximum storm surge forecast for 27 August 2026 at 17:00 UTC.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for SAUDEL-26 (active from 18 August to 26 August 2026) rates the storm an overall Green alert -- 'a low humanitarian impact based on the maximum sustained wind speed, exposed population and vulnerability' -- with maximum sustained winds of '213 km/h Category 4', approximately 280,000 people in Category 1 or higher wind zones across Japan and the Northern Mariana Islands, and a maximum storm surge of 1.8 metres.

GDACS's event-data API (episode 36) for SAUDEL-26 records an overall Orange alert with the event window extended to 18 August 2026 12:00 UTC - 27 August 2026 06:00 UTC, unchanged maximum sustained winds of 213 km/h (Category 4), about 11.5 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher winds across Japan, China and the Northern Mariana Islands, and a maximum storm surge of 2.3 metres (forecast for 28 August 00:00 UTC).

description: Tropical Cyclone Saudel intensified to Category 4 strength (213 km/h sustained winds) in the Philippine Sea in mid-August 2026, tracking toward Japan's Ryukyu Islands after affecting the Northern Mariana Islands. GDACS lowered the storm to a Green alert on 26 August as it appeared to weaken, then re-escalated it to an overall Orange alert on 27 August as its episode window extended to 27 August with unchanged Category 4 intensity (213 km/h), about 11.5 million people now exposed to Category 1 or higher winds across Japan, China and the Northern Mariana Islands (up from about 280,000), and a forecast maximum storm surge of 2.3 m. No death, injury or displacement figure has been confirmed by an authoritative source.

impact.summary: GDACS re-escalated SAUDEL-26 to an overall Orange alert (medium humanitarian impact) on 27 August 2026, with its episode window extended to 27 August, unchanged Category 4 intensity (213 km/h), about 11.5 million people now exposed to Category 1 or higher winds across Japan, China and the Northern Mariana Islands (up sharply from about 280,000 at the 26 August Green assessment), and a forecast maximum storm surge of 2.3 m. No death, injury or displacement figure has been confirmed by an authoritative source.

location.region: Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa / Amami Ōshima), extending to China

event.scale: Category 4 peak (213 km/h); GDACS re-escalated to Orange as of 27 August 2026

name: Typhoon Saudel — Northern Mariana Islands, Japan & China

updates.text: GDACS re-escalated SAUDEL-26 from Green back to an overall Orange alert as its episode window extended to 27 August, with exposed population rising to about 11.5 million people across Japan, China and the Northern Mariana Islands (from about 280,000) and a forecast maximum storm surge of 2.3 m.

GDACS lowered SAUDEL-26 to an overall Green alert (low humanitarian impact) for its 18-26 August track, with about 280,000 people in Category 1 or higher wind zones across Japan and the Northern Mariana Islands (from about 3.5 million at the 24 August Orange assessment) and a maximum storm surge of 1.8 m.
